name: gitsync.md
ctaMessage: You've started but agents are leaving you on the table.
agenticSummary: Gitsync.md offers strong Git access control integration, but lacks WebMCP support for agent discovery.

checks.name: ARD discovery
checks.details: No /.well-known/ard.json, no same-site rel="ard" link, and no legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agentic Resource Discovery catalog at /.well-known/ard.json so AI clients can discover your agentic resources (MCP servers, agents, skills, APIs). See https://agenticresourcediscovery.org/

checks.name: AI Catalog discovery
checks.details: No /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - the AI Catalog Standard's discovery path. Bonus only; a catalog at /.well-known/ard.json is scored by the ARD discovery check.
checks.recommendation: Serve a valid catalog at /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - the AI Catalog Standard's own discovery path - so consumers following that spec (see https://ai-catalog.io/) also find you. The entries can be the same as in /.well-known/ard.json, but this standard's document also needs "specVersion": "1.0" at the top level.

checks.name: ARD entry validity
checks.details: No catalog at /.well-known/ard.json, a rel="ard" link, or /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - entry validity applies only to published catalogs
checks.recommendation: Make every catalog entry fully valid: a domain-anchored urn:air identifier, a displayName, a media type, and exactly one of url or data. Applies to the catalog at /.well-known/ard.json, behind a rel="ard" link, or at the legacy /.well-known/ai-catalog.json.

checks.name: ARD trust manifest
checks.details: No catalog at /.well-known/ard.json, a rel="ard" link, or /.well-known/ai-catalog.json - trust metadata applies only to published catalogs
checks.recommendation: Add a trustManifest (verifiable identity, compliance attestations, or signature) to your catalog entries (ard.json, a rel="ard" source, or the legacy ai-catalog.json) so clients can verify your resources with progressive trust.

checks.name: Category share of voice
checks.details: Category share of voice is in beta. It measures whether agents surface you for capability and use-case searches (not just your name). We are tuning it for accuracy before it counts toward your score - coming soon as a Pro check.
checks.recommendation: Build topical authority for your category. Publish comparison pages, 'best X for Y' content, tutorials, and integration guides that rank for generic use-case queries - not just your brand name - so agents surface you when users describe a need.

checks.name: Developer resource discoverability
checks.details: Agent searched for "gitsync" developer resources but found nothing relevant
checks.recommendation: Check whether your developer resources (API docs, OpenAPI spec, auth docs, developer portal, MCP server, SDK documentation) surface in name-based searches. If they do not, use predictable URLs, link them in llms.txt, and include your product name in page titles and headings. This result reflects one search sample.
checks.naReason: no developer resources exist for agents to find by name

checks.name: Brand name discoverability
checks.details: gitsync.md was not in the top 10 for "gitsync Git client"
checks.recommendation: Make sure your own domain ranks in the top results when people search your brand together with your main product (for example "Acme payments API"). If it does not, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen it by describing your main product clearly in your homepage title and headings, earning press mentions that link to your domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask your main domain in search results.

checks.name: Wikipedia / Wikidata entity presence
checks.details: No Wikipedia article or Wikidata entity found for "gitsync" - creating a Wikipedia page and a Wikidata item with P856 = gitsync.md is the highest-impact step for AI search citation coverage
checks.recommendation: Establish a Wikipedia article and a Wikidata entity for your brand, with the domain set as the official website (Wikidata property P856) and a corresponding external link on Wikipedia. Wikipedia is the largest single source of citations in ChatGPT and a primary input to Knowledge Graphs across Google, Bing, and LLM training data. Earn third-party press coverage first to satisfy notability, then draft the article with cited references rather than self-promotion.

checks.name: robots.txt AI crawler policy
checks.details: AI search crawlers: allowed in 18 of 18 checks (3 crawlers on 6 pages). AI training crawlers: allowed in 12 of 12 checks (2 crawlers on 6 pages), not scored. No applicable crawl or usage restriction found for 3 search crawlers (oai-searchbot, claude-searchbot, perplexitybot) on 6 public pages: https://gitsync.md/, https://gitsync.md/about, https://gitsync.md/blog/git-lfs-ios, https://gitsync.md/blog/obsidian-git-iphone-ipad, https://gitsync.md/blog/self-hosted-git-ssh-ios, https://gitsync.md/compare/obsidian-sync-vs-git. Declared policy only; absence of a Content Signal expresses no usage preference. Paths outside this sample, live bot access, indexing, and model training are not verified
checks.recommendation: In robots.txt, allow the AI search crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) to read your public pages, so AI search can find and cite them. The result shows which pages and which robots.txt lines block them. Keep private and account pages blocked. Blocking AI training crawlers such as GPTBot and ClaudeBot is your choice and never lowers this score. Visits that people ask an AI to make are covered by a separate check.

checks.name: NPM/PyPI SDK package
checks.details: No NPM or PyPI SDK package found
checks.recommendation: Publish a JavaScript/TypeScript SDK package on npm so developers can integrate your API programmatically. In package.json set `repository` to your source repo and `homepage` to your product domain - these links are how agents confirm the package is your official SDK rather than a third-party tool with a similar name.
checks.naReason: no JS SDK needed; product has no developer audience or public API

checks.name: Agent platform configs
checks.details: Could not locate a public repo containing agent configs or rules. If our probes missed it, AI coding agents likely will too - link the repo from your homepage or docs so it's discoverable.
checks.recommendation: Add an AGENTS.md or .cursorrules file to your public GitHub repo with instructions for how AI coding agents should interact with your codebase. Then make sure the repo is documented in the entry-point pages agents read - homepage, docs, and llms.txt - so it can be discovered without guessing.

checks.name: Agent Plugins manifest
checks.details: No Agent Plugins manifest (plugin.json) found in discovered repos
checks.recommendation: Bundle your agent skills and MCP servers as an Agent Plugin: add a plugin.json manifest with the agent-plugins.org $schema and a name. See https://agent-plugins.org/specification

checks.name: Registry branding
checks.details: No MCP server detected
checks.recommendation: Give your MCP server-card (at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json) a display name, an icon or logo, and a description - all three together are what reads as a complete, branded listing agents can present.

checks.name: ChatGPT app listed
checks.details: Not found in ChatGPT app directory
checks.recommendation: Submit your app to the ChatGPT apps / connectors directory (the apps-in-ChatGPT surface) so ChatGPT users can discover and use your product.

checks.name: Homepage not hidden from search
checks.details: No noindex on the homepage: no robots, googlebot or bingbot meta tag and no X-Robots-Tag header hides it from search.
checks.recommendation: Remove the noindex directive from your homepage: the robots, googlebot or bingbot meta tag in the page head, or an X-Robots-Tag response header. Common causes are a staging setting left on after launch (in WordPress, Settings > Reading > Discourage search engines), an SEO plugin setting, or a host adding the header, as preview builds often do. Verify with `curl -sI https://yourdomain.com | grep -i x-robots-tag` and by searching the page source for name="robots".

checks.name: Sitemap exists
checks.details: Valid sitemap found at https://gitsync.md/sitemap.xml with 21 entries
checks.recommendation: Add a valid XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml listing all indexable URLs. Include lastmod dates and keep it under 50MB.

checks.name: Content without JavaScript
checks.details: 7735 chars, semantic headings (1 H1 + 7 H2s + 12 H3s), 28.9% content ratio
checks.recommendation: Serve at least 500 characters of meaningful homepage content in raw HTML. Add a clear H1, keep deeper heading levels sequential, and remove excessive non-content markup.

checks.name: Not blocked by bot detection
checks.details: Site accessible to 4 agent user-agents (ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot).
checks.recommendation: Let the agents that act for users and search (ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot) through your WAF and bot rules. On Cloudflare, allow verified bots rather than matching User-Agent strings, which anyone can fake.

checks.name: Agent discovery file
checks.details: No agent discovery file found
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent Skills index at /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json that lists your capabilities, with each skill carrying a name and a description so agents can find and parse what you offer.

checks.name: Agent Skills index conformance (v0.2.0)
checks.details: No /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json - skip v0.2.0 conformance
checks.recommendation: Upgrade /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json to the v0.2.0 schema: add "$schema": "https://schemas.agentskills.io/discovery/0.2.0/schema.json", and give every entry a type (skill-md or archive), url, and digest. Use "digest": "sha256:<64 lowercase hex chars>" (e.g. "digest": "sha256:a3f1...") - a bare "sha256": "<hex>" field is also accepted. Compute the value from the artifact's raw bytes. For archives, hash the ZIP or tar.gz download itself; a separate skill-md entry is not required.

checks.name: A2A / agent-card
checks.details: No A2A agent card found at /.well-known/agent-card.json
checks.recommendation: Publish an Agent-to-Agent (A2A) agent card at /.well-known/agent-card.json describing your agent's capabilities, skills, and contact endpoint.

checks.name: Listed on skills.sh
checks.details: No official skills self-published on skills.sh (87 community skills with potential relation to this domain found, but only self-published official skills count)
checks.recommendation: Publish agent skills on skills.sh so AI agents can discover your product's capabilities. Create a SKILL.md in your GitHub repo and register it with 'npx skills add'. See skills.sh/docs.

checks.name: pricing.md exists
checks.details: Structured pricing.md found at /pricing.md (12 lines)
checks.recommendation: Create a /pricing.md file with your pricing tiers, features, and limits in plain markdown. This lets AI agents compare costs and recommend plans without scraping HTML pricing pages.

checks.name: NLWeb Schema Feeds
checks.details: No schemamap: directive in robots.txt
checks.recommendation: Add a schemamap: directive to robots.txt pointing to a Schema Map XML file listing your structured data feeds (JSONL/RSS). See the NLWeb Schema Feeds spec.

checks.name: MCP well-known discovery
checks.details: No MCP server URL discovered
checks.recommendation: List each MCP server's card, hosted on your own domain, in /.well-known/ai-catalog.json, the document MCP clients fetch for discovery (ARD crawlers read the same catalog at /.well-known/ard.json), and serve the card at <server URL>/server-card, or name the server URL in llms.txt, so agents can find the server without anyone typing its URL in.

checks.name: Agent mode view
checks.details: Agent mode view found at ?mode=agent (2 signals: agent, integration)
checks.recommendation: Add a ?mode=agent query parameter to your homepage that returns a structured, machine-readable view with API endpoints, authentication info, and key capabilities instead of marketing HTML.

checks.name: HTTP Link headers (RFC 8288)
checks.details: No HTTP Link response headers (RFC 8288) found
checks.recommendation: Add HTTP Link: response headers (RFC 8288) advertising your sitemap, markdown alternates, API service descriptions, and API catalog. Example: Link: </sitemap.xml>; rel="sitemap", </index.md>; rel="alternate"; type="text/markdown".

checks.name: Markdown URL fallback
checks.details: Full markdown fallback support. Homepage (https://gitsync.md/index.md) and all 3 sampled content pages return markdown: https://gitsync.md/about.md, https://gitsync.md/blog/git-lfs-ios.md, https://gitsync.md/blog/obsidian-git-iphone-ipad.md
checks.recommendation: Let agents fetch markdown by appending .md to page URLs. Required for any credit: serve a markdown homepage at /index.md. For full credit (2/2): also serve a .md twin for each content page (e.g. /docs/auth -> /docs/auth.md). Content-Type should be text/markdown and the body should start with a top-level heading (not HTML).

checks.name: Modular llms.txt per product area
checks.details: No section-level llms.txt found. Tried /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt, /developers/llms.txt, /guides/llms.txt, /reference/llms.txt, /blog/llms.txt. This is a bonus check: it can add a point and never costs one.
checks.recommendation: Add an llms.txt file for each main section of your site (for example /docs/llms.txt or /blog/llms.txt) and link each one from your root llms.txt, so an agent working in one area can fetch a focused index instead of the whole site.

checks.name: Sitemap freshness (lastmod)
checks.details: 100% of 21 sampled sitemap entries carry lastmod; newest is 1 day(s) old
checks.recommendation: Add <lastmod> dates (W3C datetime, e.g. 2026-08-01) to your sitemap entries and update them when content actually changes. Aim for lastmod on at least half your entries with the newest within the last year. Verify with `curl https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml | grep lastmod`.

checks.name: robots.txt agent-user policy
checks.details: No applicable crawl or usage restriction found for 3 user-triggered agents (chatgpt-user, claude-user, perplexity-user) on 1 public page: https://gitsync.md/. Declared policy only; absence of a Content Signal expresses no usage preference. Paths outside this sample, live bot access, indexing, and model training are not verified
checks.recommendation: Review the matched homepage rules for ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, and Perplexity-User. If you intend to permit these requests, remove or narrow the reported restriction while keeping private paths protected. Review applicable ai-input=no declarations if answer-time use is intended. This check reports declared permission; a robots.txt change alone does not establish live access.

checks.name: llms.txt exists
checks.details: Found the llms.txt at https://gitsync.md/llms.txt.
checks.recommendation: Create an llms.txt file at your domain root (/llms.txt) - the AI equivalent of robots.txt. Write at least 100 characters of real content: what your product is, what it does, and links to your key docs. Then verify it with `curl https://yourdomain.com/llms.txt` - you should see your text, not HTML. If your app returns its homepage for every URL (common with single-page apps), add a static file route so the raw text is served. A placeholder with just a heading earns no credit.

checks.name: llms.txt formatting
checks.details: The llms.txt is well-formatted: 24 lines with markdown links, 2,930 characters in total.
checks.recommendation: Format your llms.txt as a navigation index: start with a markdown heading, include markdown links to deeper resources, and keep it under 30,000 characters. If you have more to say, move long-form content into /llms-full.txt or per-section files (e.g. /docs/llms.txt, /api/llms.txt) and link to them from the main index.

checks.name: JSON-LD structured data
checks.details: Rich JSON-LD identity: SoftwareApplication with name, description, url, and category/offers (1 block(s))
checks.recommendation: Add JSON-LD structured data to your homepage using the identity type that matches your site - SoftwareApplication for products, Organization or LocalBusiness for companies, Person for personal sites, Article for blogs - with name, description, url, and type-appropriate fields (offers, sameAs, author) so AI can parse your identity programmatically.

checks.name: Pricing info accessible
checks.details: Pricing structured data (schema.org/Offer) found
checks.recommendation: Make pricing discoverable - add a /pricing page or include pricing as schema.org/Offer structured data, so agents can find it without scraping a marketing page.

checks.name: Public API/docs linked from homepage
checks.details: No public API or documentation page linked from homepage
checks.recommendation: Publish API documentation at a discoverable URL (/docs, /api, /developers). Include authentication, endpoints, and example requests.
checks.naReason: no developer surface to document or link from the homepage

checks.name: Agent instruction / when-to-use
checks.details: When-to-use guidance found in llms.txt
checks.recommendation: Tell agents when to reach for you: add a 'when to use this' section to your llms.txt (or a dedicated agent-instructions file) that names your best-fit use cases and how an agent should call you. Be specific about the jobs you are right for - generic marketing copy does not read as guidance.

checks.name: Skills.sh skill quality
checks.details: No official skills on skills.sh to evaluate
checks.recommendation: Expand your skills.sh presence with multiple skill repos covering different use cases. Add descriptive skill names, clear SKILL.md files, and organize by capability area.

checks.name: JSON-LD entity linking (sameAs)
checks.details: Entity linking to github.com  - add more authority profiles (Wikipedia, Wikidata, LinkedIn, GitHub)
checks.recommendation: Add sameAs links in your JSON-LD structured data pointing to your Wikipedia page, Wikidata entry, GitHub org, and social profiles. This helps AI disambiguate your brand from similarly named entities.

checks.name: Metadata completeness
checks.details: All metadata signals present: canonical URL, lang="en", og:image, og:type
checks.recommendation: Add all four signals to your homepage: <link rel="canonical">, <html lang="...">, <meta property="og:image">, and <meta property="og:type">. Agents use these for entity resolution and attribution.

checks.name: Organization schema completeness
checks.details: Site identifies as a person (Person schema present) - Organization schema is not applicable
checks.recommendation: Add Organization JSON-LD that includes both contactPoint (with email/phone and contactType) and address (PostalAddress). This lets AI verify your business legitimacy and answer contact queries.

checks.name: Schema type breadth
checks.details: No extended schema types found - AI can only answer basic questions about this entity
checks.recommendation: Expand your JSON-LD beyond Organization/WebSite with more schema.org types that match what your homepage shows. Only add a type where the page shows that content.

checks.name: Trust anchor pages
checks.details: All trust anchor pages verified: About, Contact, Privacy
checks.recommendation: Publish real /about, /contact, and /privacy pages with at least 500 characters of content each. These are the pages AI agents check to verify your business is legitimate before recommending you.

checks.name: llms.txt links resolve
checks.details: All 5 probed llms.txt links resolve to real content
checks.recommendation: Make every link your llms.txt declares resolve to real content. Verify each one with `curl -L <url>` - you should see the linked document, not your homepage. If your app returns the homepage shell for unknown paths (common with single-page apps), a 200 status is not proof: check the body. Fix or remove any dead link; agents that follow the index treat a broken link as a dead end.

checks.name: Markdown alternate link
checks.details: No sampled page advertises a markdown alternate. Add <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="..."> (or the equivalent Link response header) pointing at a markdown twin of the page.
checks.recommendation: Advertise a markdown twin of each page with <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="..."> in the HTML head (or an equivalent Link response header), and make sure the advertised URL actually serves markdown - an advertisement pointing at HTML is worse than none. Verify the target with `curl -s <href>` and check the body starts with a heading, not <!doctype html>.

checks.name: Markdown frontmatter metadata
checks.details: None of the 1 served markdown doc opens with a --- frontmatter block. Add title, description, canonical, and last-updated so agents get metadata without scraping.
checks.recommendation: Open your served markdown docs with a --- frontmatter block carrying title plus at least one of description, canonical, or last-updated. Agents read frontmatter as document metadata without scraping. A Link: rel="canonical" response header also satisfies the canonical slot.

checks.name: Redirect hygiene
checks.details: No meta-refresh stubs, JavaScript-redirect stubs, or cross-domain hops across 6 checked pages
checks.recommendation: Replace meta-refresh and JavaScript-only redirects with real HTTP 301/302 redirects. Non-JS agents never execute `location.href` or wait for a meta refresh - they see only the stub page. Verify with `curl -sI <url>` - you should see a Location header, not a 200 with a near-empty body.

checks.name: Page token budget
checks.details: All 7 measured pages fit an agent context budget (largest ~3K tokens)
checks.recommendation: Keep each page's extracted text under ~100K characters (~25K tokens) so it fits an agent's context window without truncation. Split oversized reference pages into focused per-topic documents and link them from an index. Check a page with `curl -s <url> | wc -c` and remember agents read the extracted text, not the raw HTML.

checks.name: Code fence validity
checks.details: Code fences balanced across 1 markdown document
checks.recommendation: Close every fenced code block (``` or ~~~) in your served markdown. CommonMark treats everything after an unclosed fence as code, so an agent parsing the document silently loses the rest of it. Count fence lines per file - the total must be even.

checks.name: Content behind auth
checks.details: All 5 sampled pages are publicly readable (5 with substantive content)
checks.recommendation: Serve your content pages without a login wall. Agents cannot complete auth flows while browsing - a 401/403 or a login-form page is invisible content. Keep public documentation public; if some content must stay gated, publish an ungated summary so agents can still represent it.

checks.recommendation: Publish an OpenAPI (Swagger) specification at /openapi.json or /api/openapi.yaml. This is how agents understand your API surface automatically.

checks.name: API catalog (RFC 9727)
checks.details: No /.well-known/api-catalog found (RFC 9727)
checks.recommendation: Publish an API catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog per RFC 9727. Serve it with Content-Type: application/linkset+json;profile="https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9727" and include a 'linkset' array with item entries pointing to your OpenAPI specs and service descriptions.

checks.name: Markdown agent docs
checks.details: Path-suffix markdown docs served with text/markdown content-type: /index.md
checks.recommendation: Pick one: (a) return Content-Type: text/markdown on GET <homepage> when the request sends Accept: text/markdown, or (b) publish a static /llms.md, /auth.md, or /agents.md file at your root with real markdown content. Option (b) is usually a single static file. This is the cold-discovery path for agents that land at your homepage from web search without reading llms.txt first.

checks.name: Markdown content negotiation (acceptmarkdown.com)
checks.details: Canonical URL serves text/markdown and text/html via Accept negotiation with Vary: Accept
checks.recommendation: Enable Markdown negotiation on the scanned homepage. Supporting it only on /docs or a separate .md URL does not satisfy this check. Requests with Accept: text/markdown must receive a nonempty Markdown body with Content-Type: text/markdown and Vary: Accept. Keep serving HTML for Accept: text/html. Adding Vary alone does not create a Markdown response. Verify both with `curl -sS -L -i -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://yourdomain.com/` and `curl -sS -L -i -H 'Accept: text/html' https://yourdomain.com/`. Check the final response headers and body: Markdown with Vary: Accept for the first request, HTML for the second.

checks.name: Bot-UA markdown serving
checks.details: No probed bot User-Agent (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User) receives markdown when requesting HTML. Optional: detect AI-bot UAs server-side and serve them a markdown representation directly.
checks.recommendation: Optionally detect AI-bot User-Agents (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) server-side and serve them a markdown representation of the page directly, even when they send Accept: text/html. Verify with `curl -A "ClaudeBot/1.0" https://yourdomain.com/` - a markdown body earns this bonus. Accept-header negotiation is scored separately.

checks.name: Personal Agent Protocol discovery file
checks.details: Not published
checks.recommendation: Publish a Personal Agent Protocol discovery file at /.well-known/poppy.json on the exact host agents request, served over HTTPS as a JSON object. Set protocol_version to "0.2" (the current draft, still in progress), set organization.domain to the host that serves the file (after any redirect, with www. if that host has it), describe at least one interface (agent, apis, or web), and name your OAuth issuer in auth.issuer whenever you list agent or apis entries, a feedback endpoint, or a web.browser_session_endpoint. Every URL in the file must be https://. Spec: https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/spec

checks.name: PAP issuer binding
checks.details: Not published
checks.recommendation: Serve RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata for the issuer named in poppy.json at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (inserted before the issuer's path when it has one). The metadata `issuer` must match auth.issuer exactly, `poppy_domains` must list this domain, and it must advertise token_endpoint and revocation_endpoint, plus authorization_endpoint when you offer direct sign-in and device_authorization_endpoint when you offer device sign-in. If you list dpop_signing_alg_values_supported, include ES256. Give every domain whose poppy.json names this issuer the same auth block. Send cache headers, and list only S256 in code_challenge_methods_supported. Spec: https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/spec

checks.name: PAP API and agent entries
checks.details: Not published
checks.recommendation: Complete every interface entry in poppy.json: each agent.protocols entry needs a type and an https:// endpoint, and each apis entry needs a type (openapi or mcp), a url, and a description. Point OpenAPI entries at a document that parses as OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1, and have each MCP server publish RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata whose authorization_servers includes your auth.issuer (and, if it lists dpop_signing_alg_values_supported, ES256). Spec: https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/spec

checks.name: PAP endpoints reject unauthenticated agents
checks.details: Not published
checks.recommendation: Reject unauthenticated agents in the shape PAP defines. Your token endpoint should answer a session request (the RFC 7523 JWT grant) it cannot verify with one of the codes the spec lists: invalid_client (401), invalid_grant (400), or invalid_dpop_proof (400) when the DPoP proof is missing. The conversation endpoint should return 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate: DPoP` challenge when no token is sent, and an MCP server that needs a token should answer a request without one with 401 and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<your /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource URL>"`, plus a DPoP challenge with the same resource_metadata when the server supports DPoP. The browser_session_endpoint should answer an invalid assertion with 400 and set no cookie, the operations endpoint should return 401 without a token, and a feedback endpoint should refuse a report sent with no token with 401 and a `WWW-Authenticate: DPoP` challenge. Answer the token, API, conversation, feedback and operations endpoints at the address you publish, without redirects, and require a DPoP proof with every token endpoint request and every request that carries a Session Token. The exception is an MCP server that does not support DPoP: requesting its Bearer token, and using it, needs no proof. Revocation and device authorization requests are neither, so they need no proof. Spec: https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/spec

checks.name: PAP agrees with ARD and auth.md
checks.details: Not published
checks.recommendation: Keep poppy.json consistent with your other agent surfaces: list the same MCP server and organization as your ARD catalog (/.well-known/ard.json), name the same OAuth issuer that your protected-resource metadata lists in authorization_servers, and, when one issuer serves both PAP and auth.md, list every grant both protocols send to its token endpoint in grant_types_supported. Publish a poppy.json naming the same issuer on every domain listed in poppy_domains, and point every 401 at the same resource_metadata URL. Spec: https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/spec

checks.details: No MCP server card found (checked /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, the site's ai-catalog.json, servers[].card in mcp.json, and <server>/server-card)
checks.recommendation: Publish a server card for each MCP server (draft MCP server-card extension). List each card in /.well-known/ai-catalog.json, or serve it at <server URL>/server-card. /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json is still read for a site with one server, but the extension does not recommend it. Include name, description, and version, and put the server's exact address in remotes[].url (serverUrl is also read) so agents match each card to the right server before connecting. Follow the extension schema for full credit: $schema set to https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/v1/server-card.schema.json, a reverse-DNS name such as com.example/mcp, and no tools[] (agents always trust the live tools/list). Keep the description to 100 characters or fewer, as the schema requires. A card without that $schema is still read, and then an optional tools[] list completes it.

checks.name: Agent-friendly 404s
checks.details: Nonexistent paths return HTTP 404 with markdown guidance for agents - the strongest 404 contract
checks.recommendation: This check awards partial credit for a real HTTP 404/410 status and full credit when a Markdown error body is also available. If the status is already correct, keep it and add the Markdown body. Include at least 20 characters explaining the error and point agents to your docs, sitemap, or llms.txt. Verify with `curl -sS -L -i -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://yourdomain.com/some-path-that-does-not-exist`. Check both the final 404/410 status and the Markdown body, served with Content-Type: text/markdown. A correct status with an HTML error page still earns only partial credit.

Register tools with document.modelContext.registerTool() and use navigator.modelContext only as a trailing compatibility fallback. Declarative toolname forms do not count: the WebMCP specification does not define them, so register the same actions with registerTool(). Chrome's origin trial covers versions 149-156, with shipping currently targeted for 157. topFixes.name: Brand name discoverability
topFixes.recommendation: Make sure your own domain ranks in the top results when people search your brand together with your main product (for example "Acme payments API"). If it does not, your brand may be too generic, conflict with a more established term, or not yet indexed. Strengthen it by describing your main product clearly in your homepage title and headings, earning press mentions that link to your domain, and avoiding redirect chains that mask your main domain in search results.
